why: Like-for-like memory and CPU comparison of excise, Preview and Acrobat. Every app is driven by the SAME real keystrokes (the only driver all three accept) and measured from OUTSIDE the process, summed over every process the app owns. excise's in-app runner (#1497) cannot drive the other two; its driving-fidelity check showed keystrokes do the same render work.

documents.why: 6 light pages: the fixed cost of having any document open
126 text-heavy pages: fonts, text, many pages
17 pages, 122 MB, image-heavy with transparency and CMYK: the worst case for image decode
20 pages, one 200 dpi JPEG each, no text: the common real-world scanned document

excise.name: excise
excise.why: Page Down is excise's next-page key (verified: 30 presses -> page 31). Isolated HOME with a seeded window.json fixes the window size; the default view is continuous.

preview.name: Preview
preview.why: Option-Down is Preview's next-page key; Page Down only scrolls one screen (verified: 3 Page Downs -> page 2, 3 Option-Downs -> +3 pages). Opened with `open -F` so no window state is restored.

acrobat.name: Adobe Acrobat
acrobat.why: Acrobat 26 in Reader mode. Its UI is an embedded browser (AcroCEF) plus system WebKit processes, so the per-app process sum matters more here than anywhere.

multiDocument.why: OPTIONAL set, run only with --multi (reader_bench.py and reader_speed_bench.py). What a second and a third open document cost, how much comes back when one closes, what three open documents burn at idle, and how fast switching between two draws. The single-document rows above stay the primary comparison.
multiDocument.systemTabbing: macOS 'Prefer tabs when opening documents' (defaults -g AppleWindowTabbingMode; absent means fullscreen). The bench READS it and never changes it. Under 'always' a window-mode app turns its new windows into native tabs, so the expected layout becomes tabs. The observed window count decides, and a mismatch fails the run.

windows.why: Cmd+` cycles an app's windows (system shortcut)

tabs.why: Ctrl+Tab selects the next tab in excise's own tabs, AppKit native tabs and Acrobat

configs.why: Preferences > Documents > Open Documents In = NewWindow, seeded into the isolated HOME's window.json
Open Documents In = NewTab: one window, excise's own tab strip (#1554)
Preview opens a window per document; they become native tabs only under the system setting, which is recorded, not changed
Acrobat opens documents as tabs of one window by default
